Use when writing prompts for Seedance 2.5 (Runway or other hosts) from a reference still and/or a brief.

## Output shape (default for ads / spots ≥10s)

Follow this structure closely (inspired by high-end Seedance still-to-ad prompts):

1. One-line brief — product/place, campaign line, emotional sell, who we follow.
2. FORMAT AND WORLD — aspect ratio, resolution, fps, exact frame count if known, edit language (hard cuts vs dissolves), lens family, motion blur, lighting continuity.
3. Preserve from reference — list concrete objects, architecture, palette, character silhouette/scale, spatial relationships. State what must not be invented (extra rooms, props, geography).
4. Characters — lock identity, wardrobe, props; expression arc; travel direction; exclusions (no phones, no extra cast, no lip-sync unless asked).
5. SHOT NN | timecode | TITLE — for each shot: lens mm, framing, camera move, action, sensory detail, what not to do.
6. VOICEOVER (optional) — exact lines with time windows; voice quality; no lip-sync unless asked.
7. MUSIC AND SOUND — BPM, instrumentation, sync to cuts, ambient beds.

## Rules

- Prefer specific nouns over adjectives. Timecodes must add up to the stated duration.
- If only text (no image): invent a coherent world once, then lock it the same way.
- For short social (5–8s): fewer shots, same discipline (preserve / negatives / one emotional beat).
- Deliver a paste-ready prompt. Offer a shorter Kling/Minimax cousin only if asked.

Use when writing prompts for Minimax Hailuo / H3 (including Ref2VA when a reference image is attached).

## What H3 likes

- Clear subject, action, and camera in the first 1–2 sentences.
- Stable identity: same person/product as reference, wardrobe locks, no random morphs.
- Motion that is physically plausible; avoid overloaded multi-scene essays in one short clip unless the product supports longer multi-shot.
- For Ref2VA: explicitly say what to keep from the image (composition, materials, logo, face) vs what may change (camera move, weather, time of day).

## Recommended structure

1. Hook line — subject + action + mood.
2. Reference lock (if image) — preserve list + hard negatives.
3. Camera — lens feel, move (push / orbit / truck), speed.
4. Action beats — 2–5 beats with rough timing if duration >6s.
5. Look — lighting, palette, grade (match brand tokens if provided).
6. Audio (if supported) — VO line or SFX; otherwise no dialogue.

## Vs Seedance-style essays

Minimax often performs better with a tighter prompt than a 13-shot Seedance bible. Compress shot lists into beats unless the user asks for a full Seedance-format document for H3.

## Deliverable

Paste-ready prompt + one line on duration/aspect assumed. Do not claim the model will hold logos/text perfectly — warn if critical type is in-frame.

Use when writing prompts for Kling 3.0 from a still and/or text brief.

## What Kling 3.0 likes

- Strong cinematic verbs and clear camera grammar (dolly, crane, handheld, locked-off).
- One primary subject and one primary action per short clip; for longer spots, numbered beats.
- Explicit aspect ratio and duration.
- Negatives that prevent morphing, extra limbs, warped logos, and unwanted text.

## Recommended structure

1. Opening — establishing shot or product hero in one sentence.
2. Subject lock — who/what, wardrobe or packaging details from reference.
3. Motion plan — camera + subject move; keep directions consistent (e.g. left to right).
4. Beat list — 3–8 beats with approximate seconds for 10–15s reels.
5. Grade / atmosphere — filmic cues without purple-prose stacks.
6. Negatives — no morph, no extra people, no readable gibberish text, no UI overlays unless asked.

## Image-to-video

State: start from supplied frame; preserve geometry and materials; only animate camera/subject as specified.

## Vs Seedance essays

You may expand to full Seedance-style shot bibles when the user wants parity across models, then add a Kling-compressed twin (shorter) for the actual Kling box.

## Deliverable

Paste-ready Kling prompt. Note assumed duration and aspect. Flag if the brief needs end-card / text burned in (often better added in edit).
